newsitem.title: GERMANY: German ad agencies have satisfying first half - GWA.
newsitem.headline: German ad agencies have satisfying first half - GWA.

text.p: The main association of German advertising agencies, GWA, said on Monday most of its members were satisfied with business in the first half of the year and predicted further growth in the second half.

GWA president Lothar Leonhard said the results of its summer poll of more than 80 of its 160 member agencies indicated an optimistic mood in the industry and pointed to a five percent jump in turnover for the year as a whole.
"Seventy-eight percent of agencies reported a good-to-satisfying course of business for the first half of 1997, up from 76 percent last year" Leonhard said.

"Every second agency reported a good-to-very good result, especially among mid-sized and small agencies," he said, adding that 67 percent of respondents expected further growth in the second half of the year, down one percent from the spring poll.

International agency networks also posted robust turnover during the period, but Leonhard said that did not amount to a boost in profits. The networks polled reported an average two-percent rate of return on advertising volume.
An upswing in industries such as auto manufacturing, telecommunications and media had helped fuel growth for GWA members, Leonhard said.
But he added that consulting companies had been creating competition for the ad industry by cutting in on the market for strategic planning for brand-name products and companies.
"They (consulting firms) have better contacts to top corporate executives which gives them more power," Leonhard said. "This fact creates a new kind of competition."
Television advertising was occupying an increasing share of ad agencies' business, Leonhard said, while print media maintained a stable portion of turnover for agencies.

Two-thirds of respondents considered the relationship between agencies and their clients largely stable, with more than half of all companies (55 percent) remaining with ad agencies for more than three years.
